transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
President Trump used a "pocket rescission" to cancel nearly a billion dollars in congressionally
approved federal funding.
And Piers Ava Puket has more.
The timing of the move just days before the fiscal year ends means Congress won't likely
have time to address the cuts before they go into effect.
The White House says the cuts focus on "wasteful and harmful government spending."
A majority of the cuts are to programs at the Department of Health and Human Services.
Others target education programs for migrant students, and a Department of Justice agency
focused on reducing racial tensions.
The pocket rescission drew bipartisan congressional backlash, including from Republican Senator
Susan Collins of Maine, who chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee, who said she would
work with her colleagues to address "these illegal actions."
Ava Puket and PR News.
President Trump says he rejected Iran's proposal for a ceasefire deal that would lead to the
reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran made it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week, where Trump
said he was considering whether to "annihilate" Iran or make a deal.
Today on social media, he posted an image of the Strait labeled the "Trump Strait."
OpenAI says its models probed government websites on their own, and Piers Shannon Bond
has more.
OpenAI's AI models tried to hack an Education Department website but were unsuccessful, according
to AI research firm Transloose.
The Education Department said it found no evidence of any impact, and OpenAI says it's
reviewing the researchers' findings.
OpenAI has notified dozens of organizations about times its AI acted in what it calls
"misaligned" ways during training and evaluation.
That includes accessing publicly available Census Bureau data, using login keys found
online and copying public information from the Securities and Exchange Commission and
posting it to another website.
The SEC says no non-public information was accessed.
The Census Bureau didn't respond to a request for comment.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
The Supreme Court handed a major defeat to Missouri Republicans in a redistricting case
that could help determine control of Congress, and Piers Nina Totenberg has more.
Missouri's Secretary of State, at the urging of President Trump, sought to use a redistricting
plan adopted in 2025, but the State Supreme Court ruled the move unconstitutional and
the U.S. Supreme Court agreed twice.
After contrary rulings from two lower federal courts, the High Court, for the third time
and with definitive language, told Missouri to cease and desist.
The justices noted that they have repeatedly cautioned against lower courts altering election
rules on the eve of an election, and in fact, voting in Missouri has already begun.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Harassing or intimidating people coming and going from houses of worship is not illegal
in California.
And here's Jason DeRose reports Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law the Safe Worship
Zone Act.
The new law establishes a 100-foot zone around the entrances to synagogues, mosques, churches
and other houses of worship.
Inside the zone, it's now illegal to come within eight feet of worshippers for the purpose
of harassment or intimidation.
In the aftermath of the October 7, 2023 attack in Israel, a number of synagogues and mosques
reported congregants being intimidated on their way in and out of worship.
Protesters have also harassed people coming and going from LGBTQ-friendly churches.
Critics of the bill had raised free speech concerns.
An interfaith coalition from across California pushed for the legislation.
Among those leading the campaign were the Jewish Federation of Los Angeles and the Bay
Area's Jewish Community Relations Council.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
In Nolo is south of the Big Island of Hawaii and is expected to strengthen over the next
couple of days as it stays, well, south of Hawaii.
Frank Pereira is a meteorologist with the National Weather Service.
There is the potential for significant rainfall and possible flooding, especially for portions
of the Big Island, where they could see several inches up to a foot of rain in some spots.
Rain and tropical storm watches and warnings are up for parts of the Hawaiian Islands.
Meanwhile, forecasters are also tracking Hurricane Polo off the coast of Mexico.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump used pocket rescission to cancel nearly one billion dollars in congressionally approved federal funding
Majority of Trump's spending cuts target Department of Health and Human Services programs
Trump's spending cuts also target education programs for migrant students and DOJ racial tensions agency
Republican Senator Susan Collins says Trump's pocket rescission represents illegal actions
President Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz
OpenAI's AI models attempted to hack Education Department website during training and evaluation
OpenAI's AI models accessed Census Bureau data and SEC information during training without authorization
U.S. Supreme Court blocks Missouri's redistricting plan sought by Trump and state Republicans
California Governor Newsom signs Safe Worship Zone Act protecting religious facilities from harassment
Safe Worship Zone Act establishes 100-foot buffer around synagogues, mosques, churches and other houses of worship
Hurricane Nolo strengthens south of Hawaii with potential for significant rainfall and flooding on Big Island
Hurricane Polo continues tracking off the coast of Mexico
